sources.review_scope: Oral capsules SmPC sections4.1–4.6, pp3–9; all source formulations retained in PDF.

before_comparison.interpretation: Contract-case failures include missing new fields/schedules and UI grading; not a count of unique clinical defects.

findings.change: Baseline and treatment-emergent findings previously shared pathways or lacked a phase guard. Added separate timing, phase and unknown-context handling.
Former closed bands ending at ANC1.499 or platelets99 missed fractional values below1.5/100. Replaced with exact inequalities.
00334 used current counts as reduction triggers but omitted treatment-day recovery gates. Current counts now govern withholding; prior-cycle nadirs govern subsequent reduction review.
Reduction now requires documented prior dose, recovery, current counts, toxicity and stop history; no invented dose below100mg/m².
Confirmed prior stop criteria remain active after recovery; 00461 preceding-course Grade4 events do not disappear when current symptoms improve.
Cycle2 eligibility and the prohibition on late escalation were missing. Added review-only escalation with prior/current toxicity separated.
Significant hepatic dysfunction exclusion was not represented and could be obscured by no-adjustment wording. Added explicit exclusion and Child-PughC conflict review.
Older CTC/source grade pathways had been labelled CTCAEv5, including a fabricated nauseaGrade4 definition. Named source grading now carries explicit edition uncertainty; no automatic translation.
00461 Grade4 and three-week non-recovery rules were not phase guarded. Their current and historical events now belong to the correct adjuvant/concurrent pathway.
00461 explicit Irish off-label consent/hospital-policy requirements were absent from decision inputs.
Added positive-serology management, baseline/scheduled-test completeness, delayed liver injury, interaction and opportunistic infection review.
PJP finding previously targeted whole_regimen, which could imply stopping radiotherapy. It now targets temozolomide and separately reviews persistent lymphopenia.
Both assessments lacked structured source dose/phase schedule. Added distinct concurrent and adjuvant phases with six-cycle limits.

issues: Significant hepatic dysfunction is excluded, although the organ-dose table expects no adjustment in Child-Pugh C. Resolve eligibility with the specialist; this is not treatment clearance.
The NCCP advises men to avoid fathering a child for six months after treatment; the current EMA SmPC says at least three months. The patient needs a confirmed local contraception plan.
The NCCP source does not specify a CTC grading edition. The UI identifies clinician-verified source grades and does not invent a CTCAE v5 nausea Grade 4 category.
Significant hepatic dysfunction is excluded, although the organ-dose table expects no adjustment in Child-Pugh C. Resolve eligibility with the specialist; this is not treatment clearance.
The NCCP advises men to avoid fathering a child for six months after treatment; the current EMA SmPC says at least three months. The patient needs a confirmed local contraception plan.
The NCCP source does not specify a CTC grading edition. The UI identifies clinician-verified source grades and does not invent a CTCAE v5 nausea Grade 4 category.
Page 1 and the v3 amendment on page 5 specify up to six adjuvant cycles; page 3 Table 3 still says cycles 2–12. The authored plan uses six, with explicit specialist review of any extension.
The adjuvant Tables 4 and 5 retain a concurrent-radiotherapy column heading. The surrounding section establishes the adjuvant context.

The Cycle-2 escalation paragraph permits preceding-cycle nausea/vomiting Grade 3, while the current-toxicity table delays for Grade 3. Previous and current grades are entered separately; escalation remains a prescriber review.

The severe-count stopping table does not explicitly distinguish nadir from next-cycle counts. A severe prior nadir is flagged for attribution review, and a confirmed prior permanent-stop criterion remains active after recovery.
This NCCP indication is explicitly outside its Irish licence. Informed consent and hospital-policy acknowledgement are required.
